{{nihongo|'''Unkanjiniimasunaramoto Shrine'''|雲甘寺坐楢本神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Yamato Province]].

'''Unkanji-niimasu Naramoto Shrine''' (うんかんじにいますならもとじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}} located in Nashimoto, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|Q131287|qid=Q131287}}{{ill|Ikoma District, Nara|Q971003|qid=Q971003}}{{ill|Heguri, Nara|Q1346790|qid=Q1346790}}. Under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|lt=former shrine ranking}}, it was classified as a {{ill|Son-sha|Q134917284|qid=Q134917284}} and is a {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=shrine receiving offerings of sacred food and heihaku}}.

=== Overview ===
In volume five of the {{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|Q1052981|qid=Q1052981|qid=Q1052981|lt=Sandai Jitsuroku}}, it is recorded: “On the twenty-second day of the tenth month of the third year of {{ill|Jōgan|Q1075635|qid=Q1075635|lt=Jōgan}} (abridged), Unkanji, unranked Naramoto Shrine, was granted Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade.”

The former shrine site was the {{ill|Chinjusha|Q13479654|qid=Q13479654}} of Unkanji Temple, about 500 {{ill|Metre|Q11573|qid=Q11573}} to the east, but when the temple was abolished in the first year of {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}}, it was relocated to its present location.

The {{ill|Saijin|Q11591100|qid=Q11591100}} is {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kikurihime-no-Mikoto}}.

During the {{ill|Edo period|Q184963|qid=Q184963}}, it was called {{ill|Hakusan Gongen|Q11579578|qid=Q11579578}} (thought to be associated with {{ill|Hakusan Faith|Q11579557|qid=Q11579557}}), and in the Meiji period it was known as Nomata Myōjin.

The subsidiary shrine on the left side facing the main hall is the Kasuga Shrine, whose enshrined deity is {{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|Q2564508|qid=Q2564508|lt=Ame-no-Koyane-no-Mikoto}}. Immediately beside it is the Inari Shrine, whose enshrined deity is {{ill|Inari Ōkami|Q719665|qid=Q719665}}.

At the offering hall outside the left fence of the shrine buildings, {{ill|Amaterasu|Q455602|qid=Q455602}} and {{ill|Hitokotonushi|Q10864079|qid=Q10864079|lt=Hitokotonushi}} are enshrined<ref>{{Cite book|Japanese|editor=Heguri Town History Editorial Committee|title=History of Heguri Town|publisher=Heguri Town Office|date=1976-04|ncid=BN04492478|pages=645-647}}</ref>.

A {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=sacred tree}} is enshrined within the precincts.
